batchName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE) - Easy Batch 2
chapterName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE)

questions.question: What practice did the famous nickname "Marius's mules" refer to?
options: Pack animals bred for the legions
questions.explanation: "Marius's mules" referred to soldiers carrying their own gear. In fact this was routine for Roman generals, not a Marian innovation.
questions.sourceQuote: Making soldiers carry their own gear, the famous "Marius's mules" (*muli Mariani*), was routine for Roman generals.

questions.question: The Cimbri, who threatened Rome from the north, came from which region?
questions.explanation: The Cimbri were a Germanic people from the Jutland peninsula in modern Denmark. They migrated together with their neighbours the Teutones.
questions.sourceQuote: The Cimbri, a Germanic people from the Jutland peninsula in modern Denmark, were on the move with their neighbours the Teutones.

questions.question: Why did Marius partly choose to serve as Metellus's right-hand man in Africa?
options: To escape a bribery trial in Rome
To avenge a brother killed by Jugurtha
To boost his chances of becoming consul
To claim Numidian lands for his family
questions.explanation: Marius joined Metellus partly to boost his own chances of becoming consul. He served as Metellus's senior officer.
questions.sourceQuote: His senior officer and right-hand man was Gaius Marius, the ambitious newcomer from Arpinum, who joined partly to boost his own chances of becoming consul.

questions.question: When Marius asked leave to run for consul, Metellus allegedly sneered that he should wait and stand alongside whom?
questions.explanation: Metellus allegedly told Marius to wait and stand alongside Metellus's own son, who was then only about twenty. Marius campaigned from the camp anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: Allegedly he sneered that Marius should wait and stand alongside Metellus's own son, who was then about twenty.

questions.question: Which body overruled the Senate and gave Marius command of the war against Jugurtha?
questions.explanation: A tribune allied to Marius took the question to the Assembly of the plebs, which gave him the war. The Senate had tried to keep Metellus in charge.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate tried to keep Metellus in charge by extending his command, but a tribune allied to Marius took the question to the Assembly of the plebs (*concilium plebis*), the popular voting body.

questions.question: In 107 BC Marius recruited the "head count" (capite censi). Who were they?
questions.explanation: The head count were men with no property at all. Normally only property owners could serve in the legions.
questions.sourceQuote: Marius instead appealed for volunteers, including veterans and men with no property at all, the so-called "head count" (*capite censi*).

questions.question: How did Jugurtha get the richer half of Numidia when a Roman commission divided the kingdom?
options: He married into the Roman nobility
He won it in single combat
questions.explanation: Jugurtha bribed the Roman commissioners into giving him the richer western half. Episodes like this convinced many Romans that their aristocratic leaders could simply be bought.
questions.sourceQuote: A Roman commission divided the kingdom, but Jugurtha bribed its members into giving him the richer western half.

questions.question: Where did Marius and his colleague defeat the Cimbri in 101 BC?
questions.explanation: The Cimbri were destroyed at Vercellae, on the Raudine Plain. More than 120,000 reportedly died.
questions.sourceQuote: In 101 BC Marius joined his colleague at Vercellae, on the Raudine Plain.

questions.question: Which Roman officer entered the Mauretanian king's camp and received Jugurtha in chains?
questions.explanation: Sulla bravely entered the Mauretanian king's camp, and the king handed Jugurtha over. Fighting alone had failed to catch the elusive king.
questions.sourceQuote: Sulla bravely entered the Mauretanian king's camp, and the king handed over Jugurtha in chains.

questions.question: In 102 BC Marius went west to confront which northern peoples?
questions.explanation: Marius went west to face the Teutones and their allies the Ambrones, while his fellow consul guarded the Alps. He crushed both near Aquae Sextiae.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius Marius, Rome's repeatedly elected consul, went west to meet the Teutones and their allies the Ambrones, while his fellow consul guarded the Alps.
